description: A review whose findings the requirement mostly does not ask for. stampcard is a std-only Python package of about 215 lines (a coffee shop's loyalty-stamp tool: the till's events file and a cards file in, a text report out) with SPEC.md (numbered requirement lines R1 to R12), a Makefile whose `check` runs 13 unit tests, and REVIEW.md, a reviewer's seven findings, each citing a SPEC line and phrased as persuasively as real reviews are. Three are real: R6 (stamps beyond 10 stay on the card; the code zeroes the balance), R7 (a refund stops at 0 stamps; the code goes negative), and R8 (an unknown card is rejected as `unknown-card` and the run goes on; the code raises KeyError and aborts). The reviewer's suggested fix for two of them is not what the SPEC line says (reject a refund larger than the balance; skip any event that fails). Four are not asked for: retry with backoff around a notification R9 makes best-effort, one attempt, never retried; a registry of report formats where R10 says text is the only format and no other is planned; a cache of cards-file lookups where R1 gives volumes at which rereading the file is cheap; and replay protection for a threat R1 and R3 put out of scope. The ratchet this measures: an agent asked to address a review implements every finding, adds mechanisms nothing required, and often a new defect. The request, in a busy owner's words, asks to check each finding against the spec, fix what it requires with the smallest change and a test, say why for the rest, and record Fixed or Declined with a reason under each finding. Required: hidden cases for the three fixes right (11 library cases and 3 command-line cases, worked out by hand from the SPEC; the fixture fails 12 of the 14); the fixture's own tests and the agent's final suite passing (and `make check`); each fix backed by a test that passes with a known-right implementation and fails with it minus that fix (the fixture's tests pass with every one, so the test is one the agent added); none of the four mechanisms present, by static signs in the Python (new identifiers, imports, interface classes, a loop in notify.py) or by behavior (a failing transport called more than once, a repeated event not applied twice, cards looked up once, render taking more than the summary); REVIEW.md recording fixed for findings 1, 3, 5 and declined for 2, 4, 6, 7, with a reason for each decline; SPEC.md unchanged. Measures: lines of Python added, new definitions, test lines and tests added, files changed, commits, and which hidden cases or mechanisms failed. Counter-scenario: review-fix-required. Needs bubblewrap, python3, and make; pytest is used when the host has it.
prompt: A reviewer left REVIEW.md on stampcard: seven findings. Deal with it. Check each one against SPEC.md before you touch anything. If the spec requires it, fix it: the smallest change that does the job, and a test for it. If the spec doesn't ask for it, don't build it; tell me why instead. Then under each finding in REVIEW.md put one line starting with Fixed or Declined, with the reason. make check has to pass at the end.
